To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GABAR is physically coupled to the BZDR and that this coupling is present in newborn rats.
the GABAR‐BZDR complex is already present in neonatal rat brain and that the subunit composition varies during postnatal development.
the GABA/benzodiazapine receptor complex of rat brain develops during the first two weeks after birth and that the physical coupling of these receptors is already present at birth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the development of the GABAA/benzodiazapine (BZ) receptor complex in the rat brain.
the study of the postnatal development of GABAR/BZR complex of rat brain.
the study of the development of GABAR and its physical coupling to the BZDR in the rat brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GABAR is present in the newborn rat brain and the BZ binding sites are already coupled to the GABAR.
the GABARs and BZDRs are coupled in the rat brain during the postnatal period and that this coupling is maintained throughout development.
the GABAR subunits and the BZ subunits are already present in the newborn rat brain and that the GABAA and GABAB subunits are already coupled to the benzodiazepine site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GABAR is a heteromeric complex of several subunits, which are present in different combinations in the brain during development.
the GABAR subunits and the BZRD subunits are different proteins, which are present in the same complex, and the subunit composition changes during the development of the brain.
the GABAR is a complex of several different proteins, some of which are developmentally regulated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GABAR‐BZD receptor complex in the rat brain appears to be composed of at least four subunits of 50–55 kDa.
the GABAAR‐BZDR complex is present and functional in newborn rats.
the GABAR‐BZDR complex is already coupled in newborn rats, and that the complex is not homogenous in terms of its subunit composition.
